messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 30 omitted, sha256 16000b8b667016d8>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Entailment
confidence: 60
reason: Clause 3.4 permits disclosure to the Receiving Party's professional advisors on a need-to-know basis, conditional on them agreeing to abide by the Agreement, and treats advisers, employees and managers as the party's agents, though the clause's literal wording 'may not be disclosed' is ambiguous and consultants are not named.
<quote check="exact">provided that that Party takes whatever steps are necessary to procure that such professional advisors agree to abide by the terms of this Agreement</quote>
<quote check="exact">professional advisers and employees, directors or managers shall be deemed to be acting</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Entailment
confidence: 55
reason: Clause 3.3 treats agents as outside the 'third party' restriction if bound by the agreement, and clause 3.4 conditions disclosure to professional advisors on their agreeing to abide by the terms, implying permitted sharing, although the 'may not' wording in 3.4 is internally inconsistent.
<quote check="exact">the Parties undertake to each other that their holding and subsidiary companies or agents shall be bound by the provisions of this Agreement</quote>
<quote check="exact">provided that that Party takes whatever steps are necessary to procure that such professional advisors agree to abide by the terms of this Agreement</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 62
reason: Clause 3.4 expressly states Confidential Information may not be disclosed to professional advisors, and clause 3.3 bars disclosure to any third party without prior written consent.
<quote check="exact">the Confidential Information may not be disclosed by the Receiving Party to its professional advisors on a need-to-know basis</quote>
<quote check="exact">will not disclose it to any third party for any reason or purpose whatsoever without the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Entailment", "confidence": 65, "quotes": ["provided that that Party takes whatever steps are necessary to procure that such professional advisors agree to abide by the terms of this Agreement", "is disclosed to a third party pursuant to the prior written authorisation of the Disclosing Party"], "reason": "Although clause 3.4 literally says 'may not', its 'Notwithstanding' framing and proviso about advisors agreeing to abide by the terms show it is meant to allow disclosure to professional advisors on a need-to-know basis, and clauses 3.3 and 8.5 also allow disclosure to third parties with prior written consent."}
